Subject: DRAFT — Light Up a Life 2026 — for Moira to review before posting

Hilary asked the other day whether we are doing the tree again this year. Her mum’s name was on it last year, and she would like to bring her sister this time. Yes, Hilary, we are, and we shall be very pleased to see you both.

Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the bookshop window again this November. Memory tags will be available in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. There will be envelopes on the counter if you would rather take yours home to write. Some things are easier written at your own kitchen table, and some are easier with a little company.

It is seven years this month since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag on the tree, I could hardly write it. These days I write it at the shop counter, with the same pen. I still have to stop for a moment, but I am glad to have somewhere to put his name.

I know I am far from the only person who feels that way. There are people we hear about often in the shop, and others whose names we only know from a little tag. You do not have to tell us their story, though you are welcome to if you would like to. And you do not have to have any connection with the hospice. The tree is for anyone who is grieving, whether your loss was recent or many years ago.

We shall switch on the lights on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing a few carols, and Doreen is making mince pies again. Judging by last year, I would not leave it too late for one of those.

Every name on the tags will be read aloud at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December, at 3pm in the day centre. You do not need to attend the service for your loved one’s name to be read.

Thank you to everyone who helped make last year’s tree what it was. It carried 412 names, and I remember people pausing at the window, looking for their own person and reading the names beside them. Thank you, too, to the children, to Doreen, and to everyone who made room for someone else on a busy pavement.

Please know that you can simply come and stand by the tree. You need not buy a book, make a donation or write a tag. You are welcome just as you are, with whoever you are remembering.

Jean
